summary: Decoded the keyboard keymap for the REVIEW WHO? / DELETE WHO? / RENAME WHO? / PORTRAIT FOR WHOM? roster pickers, which share entry point `wpcmk_show_roster_picker` (wpcmk file 0x56a0). The picker has a two-state cursor (`local_a`): 0 = on a roster row (cursor index in `local_8`), 1 = on the CANCEL row. ArrowLeft jumps to CANCEL; ArrowRight/Up/Down jump back to roster. Enter commits the current selection (PICK if on roster, CANCEL if on CANCEL). Initially RE'd with the keyboard/mouse remap direction reversed — corrected after empirical testing in DOSBox confirmed the actual behavior.

key_findings.returnValue: Selected roster index (0..N-1) or -1 if CANCEL was confirmed

stateVars.local_a: 0 = on roster row; 1 = on CANCEL row

controlGate.meaning: Mouse-input mode (NOT keyboard, as initially misread). When true, the remap block runs and translates mouse-derived codes into keyboard-equivalent codes; when false, keyboard codes pass through directly to the post-remap if-elif chain.

keyboard_bindings.ArrowLeft (1): if not on CANCEL → jump cursor to CANCEL row
keyboard_bindings.ArrowUp (2): if on CANCEL → return to roster; else cursor up (clamp at 0)
keyboard_bindings.ArrowRight (3): if on CANCEL → return to roster; else no-op (engine binding — Right is a no-op on roster)
keyboard_bindings.ArrowDown (4): if on CANCEL → return to roster; else cursor down (clamp at N-1)
keyboard_bindings.Enter (5): exits the loop; returns cursor index if on roster, -1 if on CANCEL
keyboard_bindings.Escape (0): no-op (doesn't match any post-remap branch in keyboard mode — the engine silently ignores Escape in this picker)

mouse_remap_for_reference.3 → 5 + local_a=1: Mouse-derived code 3 jumps to CANCEL and exits

scrollbar.geometry: E at row 0 (top arrow), G G G G G at rows 1..5 (track), F at row 6 (bottom arrow); rows 7..12 blank. All attr 0x02 (wfont2 glyphs).
scrollbar.purpose: Decorative — engine doesn't track scroll within this 13-row panel. Behavior for >13 entries (paging) not yet RE'd.

highlight_model.on_roster: The selected roster row's NAME at attr 0x50; CANCEL at attr 0x03
highlight_model.on_cancel: The roster row's NAME at attr 0x03; CANCEL at attr 0x50 (highlight flips)

findings.claim: The roster picker has a two-state cursor: 'on roster' (with index `local_8` in 0..N-1) or 'on CANCEL'. The highlight flips between the roster row and the CANCEL bottomBar row based on this state.
findings.evidence: wpcmk file 0x56a0 — variable `local_a` toggles 0/1; the picker post-remap chain sets `local_a` from key events.

findings.claim: ArrowLeft is the engine's mechanism to jump from a roster row to CANCEL. Once on CANCEL, Enter dispatches the cancel.
findings.evidence: wpcmk file 0x56a0 keyboard path — `if (local_4 == 1) { if (local_a != 1) local_a = 1; }`. Verified empirically in DOSBox.

findings.claim: ArrowRight is a no-op when the cursor is on a roster row; it only does something when on CANCEL (returns to roster).
findings.evidence: wpcmk file 0x56a0 keyboard path — `if (local_4 == 3) { if (local_a == 1) local_a = 0; }`. Empirically verified in DOSBox.

findings.claim: Escape has no effect in keyboard mode — the post-remap if-elif chain doesn't match raw code 0. (The remap converting 0 → 5 only runs in mouse mode.)
findings.evidence: wpcmk file 0x56a0 — keyboard path falls through code 0 with no state transition.

findings.claim: The `*0x4fc4 == 1` gate inside the input poll loop selects the MOUSE-input remap path, NOT the keyboard path. Earlier RE incorrectly inverted this.
findings.evidence: Empirical testing in DOSBox (keyboard) confirmed Up = up, Down = down, Left = jump-to-cancel, Right = no-op on roster — the post-remap if-elif behavior, not the remap output. The remap therefore must apply to the non-keyboard (mouse) input path.

port_decisions.decision: All four pickers (Review/Delete/Rename/PortraitTarget) use the engine-correct two-state cursor via the `useRosterPicker` shared hook.
port_decisions.rationale: Natural arrow-key mapping; faithful to the engine; Left to CANCEL + Enter to confirm matches what players expect.
port_decisions.implementation: screens/useRosterPicker.ts; ReviewPickerScreen / DeletePickerScreen / RenamePickerScreen / PortraitTargetPickerScreen all delegate input to it.

port_decisions.decision: Our port also accepts Escape as a quick-cancel — engine ignores Escape in this picker but modern users expect it to cancel.
port_decisions.rationale: Pure-additive UX improvement; engine-faithful path (Left + Enter) still works.
port_decisions.implementation: useRosterPicker handles 'Escape' by calling onCancel directly.

unresolved: Whether the engine's mouse-mode input has additional behaviors worth porting. Left as a follow-up if mouse support becomes a priority.
